4581.stem:
The graph below shows the conversion between kilometres and miles.

\exfigure{15_q16_1}

figures.cap: straight line graph of miles against kilometres through (0,0) and (50, 80)

parts.latex: Calculate the gradient of the line.
Use the gradient, or otherwise, to convert 150 kilometres into miles.

meta.marker_note: Miles and km were supposed to be swapped on the axes; consequential follow-through (CFPA) is allowed if working is shown.
meta.format_note: Source offers two answers because of the axes labelling; both kept.
meta.correction_note: Claude 23 Nov (Standard batch 1 verify): the papers axes were mislabelled and the guideline accepted both answers; the final line now says so
meta.edited_from_original: Printed with miles on the vertical axis and kilometres across (the marking guideline says they were meant to be swapped, and accepted 93.75 or 240). Checker 23 Nov: "switch miles and km": the graph now has kilometres up and miles across, so the answer is 93.75 miles only.
meta.solution_before_checker:
If the axes are swapped (km on the vertical axis, as intended):
$$\begin{aligned} \text{km} &= 1.6 \times \text{miles} \\ 150 &= 1.6 \times \text{miles} \\ \text{miles} &= \dfrac{150}{1.6} \\ &= 93.75 \text{ miles} \end{aligned}$$
If the axes are not swapped:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{miles} &= 1.6 \times \text{km} \\ &= 1.6 \times 150 \\ &= 240 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ 150 \text{ km} = 93.75 \text{ miles (axes as intended), or } 240 \text{ (axes as printed); both were accepted}$$
meta.checker_confirms: work/s1/verify_out_15_2.json: the checker's answer is (a) 1.6; (b) 240 miles from the graph as drawn (93.75 only if the axes are swapped)

15_q16_1.notes: Miles against kilometres: light-grey grid at every 10 km and 50 miles, axes with arrows, line through the origin with gradient 1.6 drawn to the right edge (0.9pt), point (50,80) at its true position with a fine aux dashed guide to the y-axis, and labels at the crop's positions. The low original-coverage score is only the scan's dark grey grid: the house grid is light grey, and every line, label and the point match. Rules 1,3,9,12,16,19. Checker 23 Nov fix: switched the axis labels: kilometres up the vertical axis, miles along the horizontal (the paper had them the wrong way round; the solution now gives 93.75 miles only).

5975.stem:
The relationship between British pounds ($p$) and Australian dollars ($d$) on a particular day is shown in the graph.

\exfigure{5832_q34_1}

figures.cap: straight line graph of British pounds against Australian dollars through (7, 4)

parts.latex: Write the direct variation equation relating British pounds to Australian dollars in the form $p = md$. Leave $m$ as a fraction.

The relationship between Japanese yen ($y$) and Australian dollars ($d$) on the same day is given by the equation $y = 76d$.

Convert 93 100 Japanese yen to British pounds.

solutions.latex:
Convert yen to Australian dollars using $y = 76d$:
$$93\,100 \text{ yen} = \dfrac{93\,100}{76} = 1225 \text{ Australian dollars}$$
Then convert to pounds using $p = \dfrac{4}{7}d$:
$$p = \dfrac{1225\times 4}{7} = 700$$
$$\therefore\ 93\,100 \text{ Japanese yen} = 700 \text{ British pounds}$$

5832_q34_1.notes: Line p = (4/7)d from the origin with an arrow, the point (7,4) and its label above it. Dotted unit grid, solid verticals at d = 5, 10, 15 and 20, small ticks on both axes, the p and d axis letters and the rotated title 'British pounds'. In round 2 I nudged the tick labels and titles to the crop's positions. Rules 1, 4, 11, 16.

6264.stem:
Mario's pay $P$ is directly proportional to the number of hours $h$ that he works.

When Mario works an 8 hour day he earns \$172.

figures.cap: blank grid for pay P against hours h
solution sketch: graph of P = 21.5h with points (0,0), (2,43), (4,86)

parts.latex: Find the equation that describes the relationship between Mario's pay $P$, and the number of hours Mario works $h$.

Draw the graph of Mario's pay $P$ against the number of hours worked $h$, making sure you clearly label at least 2 plotted points.

\exfigure{496_q26_1}

solutions.latex:
Direct variation is $P = kh$, so substitute $P = 172$, $h = 8$.
$$\begin{aligned} 172 &= 8k \\ k &= 21.5 \end{aligned}$$

figures.cap: option C: graph D=180T-1800 drawn as a decaying curve

parts.latex:
The distance travelled by a person walking at a constant speed varies directly with the time that they have been walking.

Jacob walked at a constant speed for 20 minutes and travelled a distance of 1 800 metres.

Which graph and equation below would represent this variation relationship?

solutions.latex:
Direct variation has the form $D = kT$, so the graph is a straight line through the origin.

Using $T = 20$ and $D = 1800$ to find $k$:
$$\begin{aligned} k &= \dfrac{1800}{20} \\ &= 90 \end{aligned}$$
So the equation is $D = 90T$.

Option A is a line that does not pass through the origin ($D = 0$ at $T = 10$). Option B has $D = 75T$, which gives $1500$ m, not $1800$ m, at $20$ minutes. Option C is not a straight line.

Option D is a straight line through the origin with $k = 90$ (it passes through about $(20, 1800)$), so it is the correct choice.

meta.self_check: k=1800/20=90; checked each option against D=kT through origin; D=90X in option D uses X for the time variable.
meta.generated_note: Option D labels the line D = 90X (X for T); treated as a typo in the source.

308_q10_1.notes: Option A of the shared option-set frame (T 0-60, D 0-5000, light grey grid every 2 min/200 m, darker every 10 min/1000 m, axis ticks every 1 min/100 m, same scale as the crop). Line D=180T-1800 drawn from (10,0) to an arrowhead at T=38.4 at 0.9pt because it meets the axis (rule 9). Label written along the line on the same side as the paper and clear of it (rules 6a/11). The stray 'B.' printed in the top-right of the crop is an option letter from the paper and is left out. The remaining colour in the overlay is the grid tone and scan stroke thickness. Rules: 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 9, 13.

308_q10_2.notes: Same frame as options A-D (rule 7). D=75T drawn from the origin to an arrowhead at T=61.5 at 0.9pt. The label is rotated along the line, above it, with a gap. Tick and axis-title fonts are matched to the crop. Rules: 1, 2, 4, 7, 9, 11.

308_q10_3.notes: Same frame (rule 7). The decaying curve has no stated equation (it is a distractor), so its shape was fitted to the crop as D = 1800 + 308/T^1.65 for T from 0.4 to 62, ending in an arrowhead. It starts at about 3200 beside the D-axis, has its asymptote at 1800, and is drawn smooth with 90 samples at 0.9pt. In the scan the steep part merges with the axis, so where it starts is estimated. The label is horizontal above the tail, as on the paper. Rules: 1, 3a, 7, 9, 10.
